newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt to meet allies on mini-budget on Tues.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt to meet allies on mini-budget on Tues.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government will hold a meeting with the hard-left Communist Refoundation on Tuesday to discuss the forthcoming mini-budget, a parliamentary leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) said.
The PDS is the biggest force in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government.
Cesare Salvi, PDS leader in the Senate (upper house), said on Monday that the meeting would bring together all forces of Prodi's ruling majority. The time of the meeting was not known.
Communist Refoundation, whose support gives Prodi a parliamentary majority, is opposed to the additional package of 1997 measures.
One of its leaders, Armando Cossutta, was quoted as telling Corriere della Sera on Monday that the party might have to take "difficult decisions" over its support for the government.
Prodi last week announced that he would soon unveil a mini-budget for 1997 to trim up to an extra 15 trillion lire ($9 billion) off the deficit.
